topic: Important Five Year Plans and Targets
description: Economic planning in India was heavily inspired by the Soviet Union model. Its primary objective was to optimize the use of national resources to achieve rapid economic growth, poverty alleviation, and self-reliance.

sections.title: Introduction to Economic Planning
sections.description: The foundational concepts of economic planning and the establishment of the Planning Commission.

key_concepts.explanation: The process by which a central authority assesses and allocates a country's resources according to defined national priorities and targets.
An economic system combining private and public enterprise. India officially adopted this framework starting from the Second Five Year Plan.

important_facts.fact: The concept of Five Year Plans in India was borrowed from the constitution of the erstwhile Soviet Union (USSR).
The Planning Commission was a non-constitutional and non-statutory body. The final approval for all Five Year Plans was given by the National Development Council (NDC).

sections.title: Early Plans and Infrastructure Development: 1951-1966
sections.description: The initial plans focusing on agriculture, heavy industries, and the subsequent 'Plan Holiday' due to economic crises.

key_associations.extra_info: The primary focus of this plan was on agricultural development and irrigation.
The primary focus shifted to rapid industrialization and basic/heavy industries.
Aimed to make the economy independent and reach the 'take-off' stage of growth.

historical_events.significance: Massive multipurpose irrigation projects like Bhakra Nangal, Hirakud, and Damodar Valley Corporation (DVC) were launched.
Major steel plants were established at Bhilai (with USSR), Durgapur (with UK), and Rourkela (with West Germany).
This plan failed miserably due to the Sino-Indian War (1962), the Indo-Pak War (1965), and severe consecutive droughts.
Due to the economic crisis, Five Year Plans were suspended, and three Annual Plans were introduced. The Green Revolution was initiated during this period.

sections.title: Poverty Alleviation and Stabilization: 1969-1990
sections.description: Plans characterized by the nationalization of banks, poverty eradication slogans, and early steps toward economic liberalization.

historical_events.significance: Witnessed the nationalization of 14 major Indian banks (1969) and the establishment of ISRO.
Introduced the famous slogan 'Garibi Hatao' (Poverty Eradication). It was terminated a year early by the newly elected Morarji Desai government.
Introduced by the Janata Party government, this plan was based on Gunnar Myrdal's model.
Marked the beginning of economic liberalization in India. Key institutions like NABARD and EXIM Bank were established in 1982.
Emphasized rapid growth in food grains production and productive employment generation. Jawahar Rozgar Yojana was launched.

sections.title: Liberalization and Inclusive Growth: 1992-2017
sections.description: Post-1991 economic reform plans leading up to the dissolution of the Planning Commission.

historical_events.significance: Based on the John W. Miller model. It saw the implementation of the New Economic Policy (LPG reforms) and India becoming a WTO member.
The central theme and objective was 'Growth with social justice and equity'.
Set an ambitious target to double the per capita income of India in the next 10 years and reduce the poverty ratio significantly.
Prepared by C. Rangarajan. The central theme of this plan was 'Faster and more inclusive growth'.
The overarching theme was 'Faster, sustainable, and more inclusive growth'. It became the final Five Year Plan of India.

important_facts.fact: On January 1, 2015, the Government of India dissolved the Planning Commission and replaced it with NITI Aayog (National Institution for Transforming India).
